newsitem.title: USA: Greenpeace activists arrested at Cargill grain terminal.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace activists arrested at Cargill grain terminal.

text.p: Five Greenpeace protesters were arrested on Tuesday for disrupting cargo loadings at a grain terminal in a protest over genetically altered soybeans, authorities said on Wednesday.
Greenpeace is protesting exports of genetically altered soybeans developed by Monsanto Co. to withstand its "Roundup" herbicide.
The environmental group claims the altered soybeans were not adequately tested before being approved for human consumption and wants them segregated from other soybeans.

A Greenpeace spokeswoman said about 25 activists protested at the loading terminal operated by Cargill Inc., the world's biggest grain trading company. Minneapolis-based Cargill handles about 350 million bushels of grain and oilseeds at the Reserve terminal each year, according to company officials.

The protesters, some in inflatable boats, plastered bright yellow posters reading "X-Genetic Experiment" on two grain ships on Tuesday before the Coast Guard set up a 500-yard exclusion zone to move protesters back, Berman said.
Five people were arrested and charged with criminal trespass, police said. Bond for each was set at $5,000.

"Our operations at Reserve, La., were only shut down for one hour on Nov. 19," Cargill spokeswoman Lori Johnson said. "It was basically a minor disruption and we chose to stop loading for that brief period for safety reasons so that the Greenpeace folks would not be injured."

Last week 17 Greepeace protesters were arrested at the Archer Daniels Midland grain terminal in nearby Destrehan, La., after nine chained themselves to the facility's gate and eight others chained themselves inside two grain barges.

Greenpeace also blockaded shipments of soybeans being imported by Cargill in Antwerp and Ghent, Belgium last week. The protests ended after Cargill obtained court orders that would have led to heavy fines had the protests continued, Berman said.
